stem: A nonpregnant adult without unequivocal hyperglycemia has an A1C of 6.7%. A repeat A1C obtained promptly is 6.6%. How should the nurse interpret these results using ADA 2026 criteria?

options.A: Both values are at or above the ADA diabetes threshold, and the second abnormal A1C confirms the diagnosis in this setting.
options.B: Both values remain in the prediabetes range because an A1C must exceed 7.0% before diabetes can be diagnosed.
options.C: A1C is useful for monitoring after diabetes is diagnosed but is not an accepted laboratory criterion for establishing the diagnosis.
options.D: Because both values are below 7.0%, the findings indicate hypoglycemia rather than persistent abnormal chronic glycemia.

rationale: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 lists A1C ≥6.5% as a diagnostic criterion for diabetes when the assay is appropriately performed. In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia, confirmation requires two abnormal results, which may be the same test at two different time points. ADA specifically notes that two A1C results ≥6.5% confirm diabetes. Therefore A1C values of 6.7% and 6.6% meet and confirm the criterion. Prediabetes is A1C 5.7–6.4%. A is correct.
educational_objective: Apply the current ADA A1C diagnostic threshold and confirmation requirement when interpreting repeated abnormal A1C results.
source_document_title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_version_date: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl. 1); live article retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Table 2.1: A1C ≥6.5% criterion. Confirming the Diagnosis: absent unequivocal hyperglycemia, two abnormal results are required and may be the same test at two different time points; two A1C results ≥6.5% confirm diabetes. Prediabetes range A1C 5.7–6.4%.
source_claim_supported: A1C ≥6.5% is diagnostic for diabetes and, without unequivocal hyperglycemia, two abnormal A1C results at different time points can confirm the diagnosis.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor and interpret diagnostic/laboratory results.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only 'only' wording and made all options parallel interpretations of the same repeated A1C results.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — ADA 2026 explicitly sets A1C ≥6.5% and confirms diabetes with two abnormal results; A uniquely matches.
